implement: legion-worker: the implementer's push, pull request body, proof on a production-like surface, review-thread resolution and handoff are this plan's T1-T6 steps.
ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass over the settled diff before the implementer's phase completes, since this change touches three packages at once.
dispatch-first: search Dispatch before filing anything, and open a dispatch ask rather than an issue for a finding outside INFRA-182.
test: legion-worker: the tester drives the real surface and reads CI for everything static, which is exactly the split this plan's section 2 names (the local listener harness for behaviour, the envoy-go job for the Go tests).
dispatch-first: a defect the tester finds outside INFRA-182 is a dispatch ask on the issue the search names, never a new issue.
review: legion-worker: review threads answered and resolved one by one, the approval of the head by SHA, and the merge gate's order.
ce-simplify-code: the standard the reviewer judges the settled diff against, including whether the simplify pass was run.

findings.finding: F1: the self-health rebuild tears down a live subscription on the first terminal probe failure (main.go:247-252, internal/bus/nats.go:341-348), so one wrong PushBound read costs the listener its delivery.
findings.answer: The probe confirms before it reports: on an unbound read it reads ConsumerInfo once more after 250 ms and returns errDurableUnbound only when both reads agree. One probe, not a grace of intervals, so the spec's first Decision stands. Plan section 3.1.

findings.finding: F2: PushBound cannot tell this listener's binding from another process's, and this repository supports two tasks of one machine id during a rolling deploy (startup_test.go:142-166), where a recreated durable taken by the replacement would read bound on the old task.
findings.answer: The unbound test is a deliver-subject comparison first: the server's info.Config.DeliverSubject against this client's own subscription subject, with PushBound beside it. Proven exact in the pod: a nats.Bind subscription's sub.Subject equals the consumer's DeliverSubject (equal=true). Needs one accessor, bus.Client.SubSubject. Plan sections 1.6 and 3.1; recorded as a spec departure.

findings.finding: F3: the intended rebind confirmation takes no context and runs inside the 10 s shutdown budget shared with the HTTP stop (main.go:911-931).
findings.answer: rebuildListenerDependencies takes the monitor's ctx as its first parameter, and the confirmation uses durableRebindInterval 250 ms with durableRebindDeadline 3 s rather than the startup pair's 2 s/135 s. The two existing callers (main_test.go:2147, :4560) move with the signature. Plan section 3.1.

findings.finding: F4: a package-level clock seam in internal/bus is a real data race: that package runs under -race in envoy-go-race and has parallel tests (socks5_test.go:281).
findings.answer: The throttle is a per-connection value with its own mutex, built inside options (which only the connecting attempt leaves on the conn), and its clock arrives through a ConnectOption, WithReconnectErrClock, in the shape of WithPublishAcknowledgementClock. ReconnectedCB resets the throttle so each new outage's first failure logs at once. Plan section 3.2.

findings.finding: F5: A2 needs an nkey-authorized server the test can stop, which testnats.StartNkeyAuthorized does not return, and changing its signature would break packages/envoy/infra, a separate Go module checked by another CI job.
findings.answer: Add the sibling StartNkeyAuthorizedContainer returning the container and the URI, and let StartNkeyAuthorized delegate to it; no caller changes and the infra module is untouched. Plan section 3.2.

findings.finding: F6: the new reconnect WARN must come from the package-level default slog, since a process test fails when a bus line stops being Go's text format (startup_test.go:598-612, the deployed metric filters).
findings.answer: Stated as a constraint on the line: slog.Warn on the package default, fields name, servers and error, in the bus's existing field style. Plan section 3.2.

findings.finding: F7: A1 asks for a run at the commit the branch starts from, and no machine in reach can run a testcontainers test outside the pull request's own CI.
findings.answer: T1 commits the one assertion expressible against base code (the health test) on its own, opens the pull request on it so envoy-go runs red there, and the fix follows; the pull request quotes that run and the head's. The other new tests exercise APIs that do not exist at base, so they land with the fix. Plan sections 4 and 5; recorded as a spec departure.

findings.finding: F8: A1's ordering (a health request landing before the monitor's next check) is a race, and its terminate is only reachable in-package.
findings.answer: A1 runs as two deterministic tests over one fixture: the health 503 with no monitor running, then the monitor's rebind, no terminate and delivery. The repository already splits that pair (main_test.go:4582-4625 beside :4533-4562). Plan section 5; recorded as a spec departure.

findings.finding: F9: a PushBound confirmation on the startup bind path buys little and costs every listener start seconds (ECS gives a 30 s startPeriod; a GCP readiness failure only delays joining the Service; every in-repo check polls for healthy).
findings.answer: Dropped: the wait runs on the rebind only, and bindListenerDurable is unchanged. This is the plan's answer to the architect's question of 2026-10-25. Plan section 3.1.

findings.finding: F10: durableProbe returning nil for every error but ErrConsumerNotFound is load-bearing and unstated; tidying it would make every transient NATS error a probe failure.
findings.answer: Stated: errDurableUnbound only when ConsumerInfo succeeds and the consumer reads unbound; every other error keeps returning nil exactly as today. Plan section 3.1.

findings.finding: F11: A6 is checkable only once the 503's words are fixed once and reused.
findings.answer: The literal is pinned: errDurableUnbound is "not bound to this listener's subscription", so the endpoint answers "durable consumer unavailable: not bound to this listener's subscription" and A6 is a grep of that string in the three documents. Plan sections 3.1, 3.4 and 5.

findings.finding: F12: R4 leaves the ERROR's multiplicity and the shutdown path unsettled; a process test greps the whole output for ERROR across ten shutdown runs.
findings.answer: One ERROR per unasked stop: the timer path and the failed-repair path share a reported flag, cleared with the timer by a successful watch install, by Stop and by End, so the ordered shutdown adds no ERROR. Plan section 3.3.

findings.finding: F13: four consumers checked and unaffected (the deploy probe skips a tick it cannot read, Dispatch's intake binds its own durables, the compose and Docker health checks only report, the goroutine-leak assertions count only End frames).
findings.answer: Recorded as the change's blast radius in plan section 7, so the implementer invents no work for them.

specDepartures.spec: Design: "durableProbe reads ConsumerInfo and returns a new errDurableUnbound when PushBound is false", resting on the Problem's "a subscriber bound there is this listener".
specDepartures.plan: The probe and the health endpoint report unbound when the server's info.Config.DeliverSubject is not this client's own subscription subject, or when PushBound is false.
specDepartures.evidence: Run in the issue pod: a nats.Bind push subscription's sub.Subject equals the consumer's configured DeliverSubject (sub.Subject=_INBOX.XRprdV4VyFO1VWPbJBK19d deliver_subject=_INBOX.XRprdV4VyFO1VWPbJBK19d equal=true push_bound=true), and a recreated durable gets a fresh inbox (durable.go:131-137). A rolling deploy binds the same durable from a second task of one machine id (startup_test.go:142-166), where PushBound alone reads true on the task that receives nothing.

specDepartures.spec: Decisions: "No grace before 'unbound' counts, beyond the three intervals the monitor already allows."
specDepartures.plan: The monitor's probe reads ConsumerInfo a second time 250 ms after an unbound read and reports errDurableUnbound only when both reads agree; the health endpoint still answers from a single read.
specDepartures.evidence: The rebuild unsubscribes the live handle before it binds (internal/bus/nats.go:341-348), and a PushBound answer is one round trip old (internal/dispatch/delivery/intake.go:557-560), so one stale read would cost delivery. The confirmation is inside one probe, so the monitor's three 30 s intervals are unchanged.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance A1: "A test recreates the durable consumer under a running listener ... The test fails at the commit the branch starts from and passes at the head, and the pull request quotes both runs."
specDepartures.plan: A1 runs as two tests over one fixture (the health 503 with no monitor running, then the monitor's rebind with no terminate and a delivered message), and the base-commit evidence is the pull request's first commit, which carries the health test alone on base code; the tests that need APIs added by this change land with the fix.
specDepartures.evidence: No test can deterministically land an HTTP request between the fault and a running monitor's next tick, and the repository already splits that pair (main_test.go:4582-4625 beside :4533-4562). No container runtime exists in a worker pod (no docker binary, no /var/run/docker.sock), so the only runner of a testcontainers test is the pull request's own envoy-go job, which runs the tree it checks out.

acceptance: A1 is proven by two tests rather than one.
A1's base-commit run is the pull request's first commit, which carries only the health assertion that compiles against base code.
